MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 8, 2021
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:02 p.m., on June 8, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on June 4, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:15 p.m.)
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Stein Mart Property 25282 Marguerite
  Parkway; Agency Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, Keith Rattay, Elaine Lister, Cheryl
  Dyas and William Curley. Negotiating Party: Kinstler Family Trust. Under Negotiation-
  Price and Terms

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigation (Paragraph 1 of Subdivision (d) )
  of Government Code Section 54956.9: Jann Kronik-Gath vs. City Council

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

City Council Minutes  1  June 8, 2021
 At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were not reportable actions.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Lisa Foto, M.V., Connie Lanzisera, M.V., and Andrea Lofy, M.V.: expressed concerns regarding
the licensed sober living home at 28312 Driza in Mission Viejo. They asked the City and Police
Services for help.

Walter Lawson, M.V.: asked what the City has planned for the 2022 Election and suggested that
the City hold a Public Hearing, so that voters have input on the next election.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: reminded the Council that the microphone belongs to the public and that the
public has the right to address the Council without fear of retribution from the City Attorney. She
questioned the role of the City Attorney and asked why he walked a closed session item on the
agenda after he already announced the two closed session items on the agenda. She questioned and
outlined the possible Brown Act Violations at the meetings of July 14, 2020 and May 25, 2021.

For the record, City Attorney Bill Curley, stated that the legal conclusions just heard were so
remarkably incorrect.

Mark Neely, M.V.: complimented Captain Vuong and stated he is one of the finest people he has
met and may be attending a ride along. Questioned the opportunities to live in Mission Viejo for
minorities.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve
the Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Goodell, Bucknum, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of May 25, 2021, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated May 14, 2021 in the Amount of $543,047.20
City Council Minutes  2  June 8, 2021

16. Annual Routine Road and Flood Control Maintenance Contract

  (1) Approved Amendment #1 to the Agreement with the County of Orange for the period July
  1, 2021, through June 30, 2023 in the amount of $2,178,990; and (2) authorized issuance of a
  purchase order to the County of Orange for the period of July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022
City Council Minutes  4  June 8, 2021
   in an amount not to exceed $1,089,495.00, pending adoption of the 2021-2023 budget by City

17. Fiscal Year 2021/22 Senate Bill 1 Road Repair and Accountability Act

  Adopt Resolution 21-16 Adopting a List of Projects for Fiscal Year 2021/22 Funded by Senate

18. Consultant Services to Produce, Direct and Cablecast Live City Council Meetings for

  (1) Awarded a contract for the subject services to Eric Winter (A21-26) for the period of July

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

22. Oso Parkway/Interstate 5 Northbound On-Ramp Improvements (CIP 16226)

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Council Members asked questions and Council Member Sachs stated he felt it was unsafe
  design for a bike lane and would not be voting if favor.

City Council Minutes  5  June 8, 2021
   Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to (1) approve
  Change Order No. 2 to Stantec Consulting Services, Inc., in an amount not to exceed $145,260
  for final design services related to the widening of the Northbound Interstate 5 On-Ramp at
  Oso Parkway; and (2) authorize the City Manager to sign the Cooperative Agreement with
  Caltrans for the Oso Parkway/Interstate 5 Northbound On-Ramp Improvements, subject to
  any technical changes required by the City Engineer.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, and Kelley
  NOES:  Raths, and Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

23. Core Area Vision Plan Update

  Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay and Director of Planning & Community Development
  Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  By consensus the City Council received the report and presentation.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

24. General Plan Amendment GPA2021-34 being a City-initiated Petition to Update the
  City of Mission Viejo General Plan Conservation / Open Space and Land Use Elements

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister and Planning and Economic Development
  Manager Larry Longenecker presented the staff report.

  Mayor Kelley opened the public hearing at 7:25 p.m.

  There being no public testimony Mayor Kelley closed the public hearing at 7:26 p.m.

  Motion made Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1) receive
  report, and (2) adopt Resolution 21-18 Approving General Plan Amendment GPA 2021-34,
  Being a City-Initiated Petition for a General Plan Update to the Conservation/Open Space and
  land Use Elements.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

25. Preliminary Consideration of Draft Update to the City of Mission Viejo General Plan
  Housing Element for the 2021-2029 Planning Period Pursuant to the Requirements of
  State Law

City Council Minutes  6  June 8, 2021
   Director of Community Development Elaine Lister and Planning and Economic Development
  Manager Larry Longenecker presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in favor of affordable housing in the City of Mission Viejo: Doug
  Harding, M.V.; Randall Simmons, M.V.; Cathy Palmer, M.V.; Ann Owens, Lake Forest.;
  Judy Fike, M.V.; Michael Schlesinger, M.V.; Sue Johnson, M.V.; Heidi Harder, Foothill
  Ranch; Keith Tuominen, M.V.; John Hanna, Orange; Beryl Lewis, Carlsbad; Rona Henry,
  Laguna Woods; Linda Tang, M.V.

  Alene Taber representing the owner, Freemont Property LLC of the property located at 23162-
  23166 asked that staff remove this property before the staff submits the Draft Housing
  Element to the California Department of Housing and Community Development for review.

  Written comment received from Mitchell Tsai, Attorney at Law stated that the City should
  require the use of a local skilled and trained workforce to benefit the community’s economic
  development and environment.

  Written comment receive from Larry Tucker for the Horowitz Group believes that a potential
  housing use on its 7-acre site at 28452 Marguerite Parkway may be feasible and would best
  be handled by an overlay.

  The following written comments were received in favor of affordable housing in Mission
  Viejo: Kate Van Camp, Laguna Woods; Cindy Ashley, Rancho Santa Margarita; Marilyn
  Schroeder, M.V.; Tommie Kozlov, M.V.; Frieda Gorelick; JoAnne Kondori; Mary Carlson,
  M.V.; Ilene Geiger, M.V.; Barb Daly, Lake Forest; Herb Cohen; Barbara McMurray, Laguna
  Beach; John Wainwright, M.V.; Alex Rounaghi, Laguna Beach; Michael Gamerl; Craig
  Johnson, M.V.; John Achee, M.V.; Julie Rampone, M.V.; John Ackerman, M.V.; Annie
  Krinksy, Lake Forest; Michelle Murphy, Orange County United Way; Aaron Hand, M.V.;
  and Cesar Covarrubias, The Kennedy Commission.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to direct
  staff to explore several potential site inventory scenarios and continue this item to the June 22
  City Council Meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

26. Fiscal Year 2021-2022 Law Enforcement Agreement and Additional Special
  Enforcement Services Provided by the Orange County Sheriff’s Department

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to (1) approve the FY
  2021-22 Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the County of Orange for an amount not
  to exceed $21,294,779; and (2) approve funding in FY 2021-22 in the amount not to exceed
  $35,000 for overtime related to special enforcement services.
City Council Minutes  7  June 8, 2021
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

27. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Sachs.

28. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Goodell.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

29. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Brian Goodell

Council Member Goodell mentioned that ten Nadadores will be leaving to Omaha to qualify for
the 2022 Olympic Swim Team. Congratulated all of them on their training and hard work.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths congratulated all the high school graduates. Stated he was excited to get
back to normal starting next week. Mentioned that the Post Office on Marguerite has excessive
weeds and he has received a lot of complaints. Lastly, he asked if Cox Communications could
give a presentation at an upcoming Council Meeting.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs had no comments this evening.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum congratulated the high school graduates. She thanked the City
Manager and Chief of Police on their hard work on the police services agreement. She also
thanked staff for their work on the Housing Element. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum wanted to
remind residents the State’s impact and over reach in our communities. She encouraged residents
to take their activism to the State.

City Council Minutes  8  June 8, 2021
 Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley stated that she has received questions from several residents inquiring when the city
pools will be open back up for children and recreational swimming. She commented that there is a
shortage of lifeguards and the city is actively recruiting and candidates will be paid $15 an hour for
the certification and on-site training. Mayor Kelley attended the ribbon cutting for Plumeria Cake
Studio on La Paz next to Starbucks. She also attended the South Mission Viejo closing ceremony
along with Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum. Mayor Kelley also attended the Capo Valley High School
Graduation Ceremony. Reminded residents that “Moor Avenue” has been renamed to “Los Lobos
Way” at Los Alisos Intermediate School. Lastly, she announced that the Community of Character
Committee is accepting applications for those student 8th grade and above and to email her if you
are interested.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:30 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Tuesday June 22, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 22, 2021

City Council Minutes  9  June 8, 2021
